approach: Define records_worktree_dir and records_root once in athena-data paths.rs beside repo_state_dir. Add RecordSet::load_from_dir and load_current (gate records.rs) and Records::from_set and load_current (store.rs), which read the worktree as plain files when <worktree>/records is a directory and otherwise fall back to the old git-tree load. Move live current-state readers to the current forms, and give read_records and walltime callers records_root. Host records_reader_scan as a cfg(test) module in xtask/src/main.rs with an explicit allow-list. Leave site.rs untouched. Test with a real-git fixture whose HEAD tree has no records/, so the fallback cannot hide a miss.

decisions.choice: Read the worktree as plain files (load_from_dir), sorted by path, with the same check_record_file and records/... relative names. Absence falls back to the old git-tree load.
decisions.reason: A scratch checkout has only the worktree and no refs for the branch. One walk feeds RecordSet and Records.

rejected.option: resolve the branch tip and pass it as a treeish
rejected.why: The branch is not in a scratch checkout's refs.
Per-caller patches are the fault the root-cause default rejects.

decisions.choice: The worktree counts as present only if <worktree>/records is a directory. paths.rs and load_current decide this in one place.
decisions.reason: Before the cutover there is no worktree, so every reader must keep its old behavior.

rejected.option: fail when the worktree is missing
rejected.why: It would break every reader before the cutover.

decisions.choice: Classify each remaining Records::load/RecordSet::load site. Live readers of current state move. Sites that judge a given treeish stay: history.rs:188 and :263, reconcile.rs, jobs.rs, attribution.rs (its own read_records(git, tip, ...)), content.rs, landing code. records_import.rs stays because it copies main's records into the branch. run.rs:361 loads right after a commit, at new_head, to judge that commit, so it stays (treeish judge). run.rs:2392 loads a head passed in as a parameter. The producer reads its callers: if every caller passes the live head, it moves; if a caller passes a candidate commit, it stays with a one-line comment.
decisions.reason: Gate checks must judge the commit under test, not the worktree. Moving the importer would make it read its own destination.

rejected.why: Gate checks would ignore the commit they judge.

decisions.choice: The scan test is a cfg(test) module in xtask/src/main.rs named records_reader_scan. It scans non-test code (each file cut at the first #[cfg(test)]) and skips test dirs, tests/*.rs and *_tests.rs. It matches join("records", read_records( whose first argument is a repo dir, and two-argument [Git]Records::load( / RecordSet::load( with any alias (Records, RecordSet, GitRecords). Allow-list by file, with a reason for each: crates/athena-data/src/paths.rs (the single definition); crates/athena-core/src/store.rs and crates/athena-gate/src/records.rs (the load and load_current fallback bodies, including the store.rs:275 fallback inside Records::load); crates/athena-gate/src/history.rs, reconcile.rs, attribution.rs, content.rs and jobs.rs (treeish judges that take a given tip); crates/athena-core/src/records_import.rs (copies main's records to the branch); crates/athena-core/src/run.rs only for the line-level treeish site run.rs:361; crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs for the root.join("records...") sites at :300/318/339/360 only if the producer finds they are fixture or label constructors, otherwise they move to records_root; crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs (copies a git tree). The invariant.rs BOOTSTRAP_OUTCOME path and the citation strings in steward.rs and work_decisions.rs are not matched, because they are not these call shapes. xtask/src/walltime.rs:83 root.join("records/jobs") moves to records_root and is not allow-listed.
decisions.reason: The mechanism enforces the single-path rule, and the allow-list is explicit so the real tree passes.

rejected.why: It would flag the citations the brief excludes.
The critic found the real tree would fail the scan.

decisions.choice: The integration fixture is a real git repo. It commits records set A in main's tree for the fallback case, and for the worktree case it commits a HEAD with records/ removed (git rm -r records, then a commit). Set B is written only under records_worktree_dir. The test also asserts the negative control: with the worktree directory deleted in the same no-records HEAD, status shows empty or different output from the run with the worktree.
decisions.reason: Live readers read git HEAD, so deleting records/ only in the working tree proves nothing. This setup fails on the old code.

rejected.option: delete records/ from the working tree only
rejected.why: HEAD's tree still holds records, so old code passes.

steps: Add records_worktree_dir and records_root to paths.rs with unit tests.
Add RecordSet::load_from_dir and load_current in gate records.rs.
Split Records::load into load plus from_set; add Records::load_current in store.rs.

Re-grep all call sites, aliases included. Classify each as a live reader or a treeish judge, including run.rs:361 and :2392. Move the live ones to load_current and the read_records callers to records_root.
Point xtask walltime at athena_data::paths::records_root (xtask/Cargo.toml already depends on athena-data) and add its unit test.
Write crates/athena-cli/tests/records_branch_readers.rs with the real-git fixture, the no-records HEAD case and the negative control.
Add the records_reader_scan module in xtask/src/main.rs with the explicit allow-list and the planted cases.
Run xtask site with and without records/ and compare; confirm site.rs is untouched.
Update docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md citing D111.
Run fmt, clippy -D warnings and the full cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: A partial or stale worktree hides in-tree records.
risks.mitigation: Present means <worktree>/records is a directory; the fallback is documented and tested.

risks.risk: Existing tests see a developer's real worktree.
risks.mitigation: records_worktree_dir derives from repo_state_dir keyed by the repo, so temp repos get their own empty path.

risks.risk: Missed call sites, including aliased ones.
risks.mitigation: The producer re-greps Records::load(, RecordSet::load(, GitRecords::load( and read_records(; the scan matches aliases and fails on any left.

risks.risk: An over-broad allow-list hides real readers.
risks.mitigation: The allow-list is by file, with line-level entries for run.rs and introspect.rs, and each entry has a stated reason.

risks.risk: Ordering drift between load_from_dir and ls-tree.
risks.mitigation: Sort by path; a test compares both loads on identical content.

demonstrations.method: The integration test drives each moved reader through a public function or a CLI command run against the fixture (records A in HEAD, set B only in the worktree) and asserts B's marker is present and A's marker absent. Mapping: Records::load_current and RecordSet::load_current are called directly. read_records is called directly with records_root. status, forecast and the steward view run as CLI commands (athena status, athena forecast, the steward command). auditor, audience, review, hestia, proposals, work_decisions and backtest run through their existing public entry points or CLI commands, as the existing tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/{auditor,audience,proposals,work_decisions,backtest}.rs do. drain uses the existing drain entry points, as in tests/drain.rs. Private readers (reading.rs, scope_guard.rs, manage.rs, run.rs, code_health.rs) run through the commands that reach them, such as plan, run, manage and code-health. If the producer cannot reach one through a command, the producer names it in the test file header, and the scan covers it. xtask walltime is covered by an xtask unit test in xtask/src/walltime.rs (cfg(test)) that builds a root, calls the function through records_root with a worktree holding B and in-tree A, and asserts B. It can also be shown by running cargo run -p xtask -- walltime against each directory.
demonstrations.observes: Every reader reachable by test returns the worktree's records only; readers covered by the scan alone are listed in the test header.
demonstrations.fails_without: A reader still loading HEAD or in-tree records returns A, and the B-marker assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: A test with no worktree asserts each moved reader's output equals the old Records::load result. A second test builds a scratch repo whose HEAD commit removes records/ (git rm -r records, then a commit) and populates only the worktree. It runs athena status and athena forecast and asserts exit 0 and stdout equal to the run on a repo with records/ in HEAD. The same test asserts that, with the worktree deleted, the output differs or is empty, which is how the old code behaves.
demonstrations.observes: Fallback equals old results; the no-records checkout succeeds from the worktree alone with matching output.
demonstrations.fails_without: A load_current that errors or returns empty when the worktree is absent fails the equality. Old code on the no-records HEAD returns empty, so the worktree-only equality fails.

demonstrations.method: paths.rs holds the one definition (records_worktree_dir, records_root) with unit tests. records_reader_scan fails on any join("records") or read_records(<repo dir>) outside the allow-list. A planted case in a new file outside the allow-list calls RecordSet::load(git, head) and a GitRecords::load(&self.git, head) alias, and must be flagged.
demonstrations.observes: The real tree passes. The planted direct read and the planted alias call are flagged.
demonstrations.fails_without: A second definition, a direct join, or a new unallowed load call would fail the scan.

demonstrations.method: The scan test has these cases: the real tree (expects zero findings), planted join("records") in non-test code (flagged), planted read_records(repo_dir) (flagged), planted RecordSet::load(git, head) in a non-allow-listed file (flagged), the same read after #[cfg(test)] (not flagged), and a citation-only file with 'records/jobs' labels and a BOOTSTRAP_OUTCOME-style path (not flagged). The output must show at least 1 test passed, not 0 run.
demonstrations.observes: 1 passed; the real tree is clean, planted reads are flagged, and citations are not.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the matchers the planted reads go unreported and the test fails.

demonstrations.method: Run the site generator with records/ present and save its output. Run it again in a copy without records/ and compare with diff. git status and git diff show xtask/src/site.rs unmodified.
demonstrations.observes: Identical output both ways; site.rs has no diff.
demonstrations.fails_without: A site.rs rooted at records/ or the worktree would produce different output when records/ is absent.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks; existing tests are not edited.
demonstrations.observes: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and the full test suite all pass, including existing tests before the branch exists.
demonstrations.fails_without: A moved reader that changed behavior with no worktree fails an existing test; lint or format errors fail those checks.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of both files.
demonstrations.observes: The entries state the reader move, the fallback, and that the site generator is out of scope, and cite D111. The existing format policy tests still pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: Missing entries or a missing D111 citation show in the diff; a malformed entry fails the policy tests.

open_questions: Whether the run.rs:2392 callers all pass the live head; the producer reads them and classifies each.
Whether the introspect.rs root.join("records...") sites build live paths or only fixture and label paths; the producer decides whether they move or are allow-listed by line.
The worktree layout is assumed to be <worktree>/records/..., as the cutover job creates it.
Whether every private reader (reading, scope_guard, manage, code_health) is reachable by a CLI command in the fixture; any that is not is covered by the scan alone.
